name: SuspendedThreadsListNetBSD::ContainsTid
prose: Const member function taking tid_t thread_id: loops over thread_ids_ (an InternalMmapVector<tid_t>) from index 0 to size()-1 and returns true at the first element equal to thread_id; if none matches (including when the vector is empty) it returns false. It does not modify the object and takes no locks.
note: Checked against sanitizer_stoptheworld_netbsd_libcdep.cpp:325-331; old prose correct.

name: SizeClassAllocator32<Config>::releaseToOS
prose: Member function taking ReleaseToOS ReleaseType: it starts with a total of 0 and loops over every size class I from 0 to NumClasses-1 except SizeClassMap::BatchClassId; for each, it takes that class's SizeClassInfo mutex with a ScopedLock (held for that iteration only), adds the value returned by releaseToOSMaybe(Sci, I, ReleaseType) to the total, and the lock is released at the end of the iteration. It returns the total of the values returned (bytes released as reported by releaseToOSMaybe). No lock is held on return.
note: Checked against primary32.h:513-523; old prose correct.

name: INTERCEPTOR(int, pthread_mutex_lock, pthread_mutex_t *m)
prose: Interceptor for pthread_mutex_lock. The interceptor first calls InitThread() and ignores its bool result (InitThread returns false while the per-thread initing flag is set, in which case the thread pointer thr may still be null). It then calls MutexBeforeLock(thr, (uptr)m, true), calls REAL(pthread_mutex_lock)(m), then calls MutexAfterLock(thr, (uptr)m, true, false) whatever the real call returned (the after-lock event is recorded even if the call failed), and returns the real call's return value unchanged.
note: InitThread() result ignored in code (dd_interceptors.cpp); lines checked.

name: INTERCEPTOR(int, pthread_mutex_trylock, pthread_mutex_t *m)
prose: Interceptor for pthread_mutex_trylock. The interceptor first calls InitThread() and ignores its bool result (InitThread returns false while the per-thread initing flag is set, in which case the thread pointer thr may still be null). It calls REAL(pthread_mutex_trylock)(m) first; only if the result is 0 it calls MutexAfterLock(thr, (uptr)m, true, true); in every case it returns the real result unchanged. No before-lock event is recorded.
note: InitThread() result ignored in code (dd_interceptors.cpp); lines checked.

name: INTERCEPTOR(int, pthread_mutex_unlock, pthread_mutex_t *m)
prose: Interceptor for pthread_mutex_unlock. The interceptor first calls InitThread() and ignores its bool result (InitThread returns false while the per-thread initing flag is set, in which case the thread pointer thr may still be null). It then calls MutexBeforeUnlock(thr, (uptr)m, true) before the real call, and returns REAL(pthread_mutex_unlock)(m) unchanged. The unlock event is recorded whatever the real call returns.

name: INTERCEPTOR(int, pthread_rwlock_unlock, pthread_rwlock_t *m)
prose: Interceptor for pthread_rwlock_unlock. The interceptor first calls InitThread() and ignores its bool result (InitThread returns false while the per-thread initing flag is set, in which case the thread pointer thr may still be null). It calls MutexBeforeUnlock(thr, (uptr)m, true) (the source comment notes that this is not necessarily a write unlock, so the event is recorded as a write-lock unlock even for a read lock) and returns REAL(pthread_rwlock_unlock)(m) unchanged.

name: INTERCEPTOR(int, pthread_cond_wait, pthread_cond_t *c, pthread_mutex_t *m)
prose: Interceptor for pthread_cond_wait. The interceptor first calls InitThread() and ignores its bool result (InitThread returns false while the per-thread initing flag is set, in which case the thread pointer thr may still be null). It obtains a shadow condition variable with init_cond(c): if the slot c already holds a nonzero pointer that pointer is used; otherwise a zeroed pthread_cond_t is allocated with InternalAlloc and installed with a compare-exchange, and if another thread won the race the new block is freed and the winner's is used. It then calls MutexBeforeUnlock and MutexBeforeLock for m (both with writelock true), calls REAL(pthread_cond_wait)(shadow, m), calls MutexAfterLock(thr, (uptr)m, true, false) whatever the real call returned, and returns the real return value unchanged. The shadow stays installed in c until pthread_cond_init replaces it or pthread_cond_destroy frees it.
note: InitThread() result ignored in code (dd_interceptors.cpp); lines checked.

name: INTERCEPTOR(int, pthread_cond_destroy, pthread_cond_t *c)
prose: Interceptor for pthread_cond_destroy. The interceptor first calls InitThread() and ignores its bool result (InitThread returns false while the per-thread initing flag is set, in which case the thread pointer thr may still be null). It obtains the shadow condition variable with init_cond(c) (if the slot is 0 a fresh zeroed pthread_cond_t is allocated and installed just to be destroyed), calls REAL(pthread_cond_destroy)(shadow), then unconditionally frees the shadow with InternalFree and stores 0 into the slot c (relaxed), and returns the real call's return value unchanged, even if it was an error such as EBUSY.
note: InitThread() result ignored in code (dd_interceptors.cpp); lines checked.

name: OSATOMIC_INTERCEPTORS_BITWISE(OSAtomicOr, fetch_or, OSATOMIC_INTERCEPTOR_PLUS_X, OSATOMIC_INTERCEPTOR) [OSAtomicOr32]
prose: Generated interceptor int32_t OSAtomicOr32(uint32_t x, volatile uint32_t *ptr) (macro OSATOMIC_INTERCEPTOR_PLUS_X with __tsan_atomic32_fetch_or and kMacOrderNonBarrier, which equals mo_acq_rel). It runs SCOPED_TSAN_INTERCEPTOR(OSAtomicOr32, x, ptr): this aborts the process if the real function was not found, and if the interceptor must be ignored (thread not initialized, ignore_interceptors set, or in an ignored library) it returns REAL(OSAtomicOr32)(x, ptr) directly. Otherwise it calls __tsan_atomic32_fetch_or((volatile a32 *)ptr, x, mo_acq_rel), which atomically sets *ptr to old | x and returns the old value, and the function returns that old value plus x (converted to int32_t). So the return value is old + x, not the new value of *ptr (old | x).
note: Round-15 reviewer right: OSATOMIC_INTERCEPTOR_PLUS_X returns tsan_atomic_f(...) + x and fetch_or returns the old value (tsan_interceptors_mac.cpp:57-62, 106-107); the old prose said (old|x)+x. The unmodified/ignored path (REAL call) was also missing.

name: dup2
prose: TSAN interceptor TSAN_INTERCEPTOR(int, dup2, int oldfd, int newfd). SCOPED_TSAN_INTERCEPTOR aborts if the real dup2 is missing; if the thread must be ignored (not initialized, ignore_interceptors or in an ignored library) it returns REAL(dup2)(oldfd, newfd) directly. Otherwise it calls REAL(dup2), stores the result as newfd2 and, if oldfd >= 0 and newfd2 >= 0 and newfd2 != oldfd, calls FdDup(thr, pc, oldfd, newfd2, false) to record the duplication; it returns newfd2 (the new descriptor, or -1 with errno set on failure of the real call).
note: Contract cleared (touches runtime state through FdDup); reviewer right that the old formal was weaker than the prose.

name: eventfd
prose: TSAN interceptor TSAN_INTERCEPTOR(int, eventfd, unsigned initval, int flags), defined only when SANITIZER_LINUX. SCOPED_TSAN_INTERCEPTOR aborts if the real eventfd is missing and, if the thread must be ignored, returns REAL(eventfd)(initval, flags) directly. Otherwise it calls REAL(eventfd), and if the returned fd is >= 0 it calls FdEventCreate(thr, pc, fd) to register it; it returns the descriptor, or -1 with errno set on failure of the real call (no registration then).
note: Contract cleared as for dup2.

name: operator new (nothrow)
prose: C++ allocation operator, nothrow (macro OPERATOR_NEW_BODY with nothrow true). If in_symbolizer() it returns InternalAlloc(size) directly. Otherwise, inside a SCOPED_INTERCEPTOR_RAW scope, it sets p = user_alloc(thr, pc, size) and does not report an out-of-memory error itself; then it calls invoke_malloc_hook(p, size) (also when p is null) and returns p. p is null only if the allocator returns null for the request, which user_alloc/user_memalign do (setting errno) only when allocator_may_return_null is enabled; otherwise the allocator reports the error and does not return. A non-null result is released with operator delete.
note: Round-15 reviewer wrong for the nothrow forms (OPERATOR_NEW_BODY(..., true) skips ReportOutOfMemory, tsan_new_delete.cpp:31-44); the old prose was already correct for the non-nothrow aligned forms.

name: operator new (aligned)
prose: C++ aligned allocation operator (macro OPERATOR_NEW_BODY_ALIGN with nothrow false). If in_symbolizer() it returns InternalAlloc(size, nullptr, (uptr)align) directly with no hook call. Otherwise, inside a SCOPED_INTERCEPTOR_RAW scope, it sets p = user_memalign(thr, pc, (uptr)align, size) and, if p is null, builds a fatal stack trace and calls ReportOutOfMemory(size, &stack), which does not return; then it calls invoke_malloc_hook(p, size) and returns p. So outside the symbolizer it returns a non-null pointer or does not return. A non-null result is released with operator delete.

name: MutexUnlock
prose: Function in tsan_rtl_mutex.cpp taking (ThreadState *thr, uptr pc, uptr addr, u32 flagz). If pc is nonzero and addr is application memory it records an atomic read of addr (MemoryAccess). It always calls RecordMutexUnlock (trace event and removal from the thread's mutex set). Under SlotLocker it finds or creates the sync object for addr and locks its mutex. In non-Go builds, if the sync object has recursion 0 or is owned by another thread, the unlock is rejected: rec stays 0 and, if flags()->report_mutex_bugs is set and the mutex is not already flagged broken, it marks the mutex broken and will report a bad unlock. Otherwise (and always in Go builds) the unlock is accepted: rec = the current recursion if flagz has MutexFlagRecursiveUnlock, else 1; recursion -= rec; if recursion becomes 0 the owner is cleared and, if !thr->ignore_sync, the thread clock is release-stored into the sync object's clock (and the epoch is incremented after the lock is dropped). If detect_deadlocks is on, s->recursion == 0 and no bad unlock is being reported (this includes rejected unlocks that are not reported), the deadlock detector's MutexBeforeUnlock is called. After the locked section it emits the bad-unlock report (ReportMutexMisuse, which does nothing in Go or if ShouldReport says no) if one was flagged; if detect_deadlocks is on and no bad unlock was flagged it calls ReportDeadlock on the detector's report. It returns rec: 0 for a rejected unlock, otherwise 1 or the recursion count removed (0 also if recursion was 0 in Go with the recursive flag).
note: Reviewers right: round 15 (deadlock detection also runs for rejected unlocks that are not reported, tsan_rtl_mutex.cpp:247-251, 259-262); rounds 1 and 2 were already reflected in the old prose (ignore_sync guard at line 241; Go always takes the accepted branch at 231-237).

name: ThreadFinish
prose: Function in tsan_rtl_thread.cpp taking ThreadState *thr (the thread finishing itself). It calls ThreadCheckIgnore(thr) (in non-Go builds it reports and calls Die() if ignores are still enabled and ctx->after_multithreaded_fork is false); drops shadow memory for the thread's stack and TLS ranges when their address and size are nonzero (DontNeedShadowFor); sets is_dead; in non-Go builds only it clears is_inited, increments ignore_interceptors and calls PlatformCleanUpThreadState. If thr->ignore_sync is false it takes the slot lock and the thread registry lock and, when tctx->detached is false, release-stores the clock into tctx->sync, records sync_epoch = ctx->global_epoch and increments the epoch; if ignore_sync is true none of that is done. It then unmaps the shadow stack (UnmapOrDie, non-Go) or Free()s it (Go), nulls the shadow stack pointers, destroys the deadlock-detector logical thread if detect_deadlocks is on, calls SlotDetach(thr), ctx->thread_registry.FinishThread(thr->tid) and finally runs the ThreadState destructor. It returns nothing.
note: Reviewers right: round 1 (ignore_sync guard) and round 15 (is_inited clear, ignore_interceptors increment, PlatformCleanUpThreadState are inside #if !SANITIZER_GO, tsan_rtl_thread.cpp:224-228); the old prose gave the first as unconditional.

name: FDRController<Version>::functionEnter
prose: Member function of FDRController (xray_fdr_controller.h), taking FuncId, TSC and CPU, returning bool. If the controller is finalized (no BufferQueue or it is finalizing) or prepareBuffer(sizeof(MetadataRecord) + sizeof(FunctionRecord)) fails, it returns returnBuffer(), i.e. it releases the current buffer and returns false if the controller is finalized or has no queue, otherwise whether the release succeeded. It then calls recordPreamble(TSC, CPU), which may write a NewCPUId or TSCWrap metadata record (and sets LatestTSC to TSC when it does); if that returns InvalidBuffer (buffer generation mismatch) it returns returnBuffer() without writing the enter record. If metadata was written it sets UndoableFunctionEnters = 1 and UndoableTailExits = 0, otherwise it increments UndoableFunctionEnters. It then computes Delta = TSC - LatestTSC, sets LastFunctionEntryTSC and LatestTSC to TSC, and returns the result of W.writeFunction(Enter, mask(FuncId), Delta), where mask keeps the low 29 bits of FuncId.
note: Previously dropped as 'not a function'; it is a member function (xray_fdr_controller.h:244-266). Rewritten from the code; the earlier reviewer's point about the InvalidBuffer path is covered.

name: controlPatching(bool Enable)
prose: Function in xray_interface.cpp (XRAY_NEVER_INSTRUMENT) patching or unpatching all objects. It returns NOT_INITIALIZED if XRayInitialized is false (XRayPatching unchanged); it returns ONGOING if the compare-exchange of XRayPatching from false to true fails (XRayPatching unchanged). Otherwise it holds XRayPatching true and resets it to false when the function exits (scope guard). For each registered object index it skips objects that are not loaded and calls controlPatchingObjectUnchecked(Enable, I), keeping a combined status that starts as NOT_INITIALIZED: SUCCESS sets it to SUCCESS only if it is currently NOT_INITIALIZED; FAILED sets it to FAILED; NOT_INITIALIZED sets it to NOT_INITIALIZED unless it is already FAILED (so it also overrides an earlier SUCCESS). The returned value is therefore FAILED if any loaded object returned FAILED (it is sticky); otherwise it is the status returned for the last loaded object (SUCCESS or NOT_INITIALIZED, so a SUCCESS followed by a NOT_INITIALIZED yields NOT_INITIALIZED), and NOT_INITIALIZED if there are no loaded objects. The ONGOING status from a per-object call is treated as unreachable.
note: Round-15 reviewer right (a later NOT_INITIALIZED overrides an earlier SUCCESS, xray_interface.cpp:408-413); round-2 reviewer concerned the per-object overload.

name: controlPatching(bool Enable, int32_t ObjId)
prose: Function in xray_interface.cpp (XRAY_NEVER_INSTRUMENT) patching or unpatching one object. It returns NOT_INITIALIZED if XRayInitialized is false and ONGOING if the compare-exchange on XRayPatching fails (in both cases XRayPatching is unchanged); otherwise it sets XRayPatching true, returns the result of controlPatchingObjectUnchecked(Enable, ObjId) and resets XRayPatching to false on exit. That callee returns FAILED if ObjId is negative or at least the number of objects, NOT_INITIALIZED if the object's sled map has no entries, FAILED if the sled map is not marked loaded (checked after the entries test), FAILED if the page size is zero or not a power of two, FAILED if making the page range writable fails, and otherwise patches every sled and returns SUCCESS.
note: All three reviewers wrong about this overload (old prose already listed FAILED for page size/mprotect and the unchanged-flag early returns); only an ordering detail (entries test before loaded test) was added. xray_interface.cpp:296-373, 422-437.

name: to_integer
prose: Constexpr noexcept function template in namespace cpp: to_integer<IntegerType>(byte b), participating in overload resolution only when is_integral_v<IntegerType>. It returns static_cast<IntegerType>(b): b is an enum class with underlying type unsigned char, and the cast converts its value (0 to 255) to IntegerType by the usual integral conversion. For bool the result is false when the byte is 0 and true otherwise; for unsigned types and signed types wider than 8 bits the value is preserved; for an 8-bit signed type a value above 127 converts in an implementation-defined way (modular since C++20). The conversion is never undefined behavior.
note: Reviewers (round 1: bool; round 2: out-of-range signed implementation-defined; round 15: no UB) all right; old prose claimed UB.

name: set_env
prose: Inline function in namespace fputil (LIBC_INLINE int set_env(const fenv_t *envp)); the slice cut the head and the item name fesetenv is not in the file. If envp == FE_DFL_ENV it reads the current FPSCR, sets the rounding-mode field to round-to-nearest, clears the six exception-enable bits (0x3F << ExceptionControlBitPosition) and clears the low byte (the exception status flags and two reserved bits), writes that value back with FEnv::set_fpscr, and returns 0; other FPSCR fields are left as they were. Otherwise it treats envp as a pointer to an FEnv, writes its stored fpscr value with FEnv::set_fpscr and returns 0. It returns 0 on both paths and reads *envp only in the second case.
note: Old prose said the FPSCR is set to the default state wholesale; in the default case only some fields change (FEnvImpl.h:240-256). Real name set_env.

name: DyadicFloat::fast_as<T, ShouldSignalExceptions>
prose: Constexpr member template of DyadicFloat returning T, enabled only when T is floating point and FPBits<T>::FRACTION_LEN < Bits; it assumes the value is normalized and the result is normal. If the mantissa is zero it returns the zero of T with the stored sign. Otherwise it computes exp_hi = exponent + Bits - 1 + EXP_BIAS. If exp_hi > 2*EXP_BIAS it multiplies the value sign * 2^EXP_BIAS by a volatile 2 (so the result is infinity or the largest finite magnitude depending on the current rounding mode), sets errno to ERANGE when ShouldSignalExceptions is true and the result is infinite and errno is enabled, and returns it; the code does not itself raise FE_OVERFLOW, but the floating-point multiplication may set hardware flags. Otherwise it forms d_hi from the top mantissa bits (a denormal path when exp_hi <= 0 uses a larger shift and sets exp_hi to EXP_BIAS), derives round and sticky bits, and builds d_lo. If exp_lo <= 0 it returns multiply_add(d_lo, round_and_sticky, d_hi * scale_up_factor) * scale_down_factor (with no ERANGE or underflow signaling). Otherwise r = multiply_add(d_lo, T(round_and_sticky), d_hi); if the output is not denormal it returns r; if it is, it subtracts the exponent bits from r's representation and, when the resulting exponent field is zero, also subtracts the implicit bit and, if ShouldSignalExceptions is true and round_and_sticky is nonzero, sets errno ERANGE and raises FE_UNDERFLOW (each when enabled), returning the value; if the exponent field is nonzero it returns it unchanged. Normal results are not signaled by this code, though multiply_add and the multiplication may set hardware inexact/overflow flags.
note: Reviewers (rounds 1, 2, 15) right in part: overflow result is 2^(EXP_BIAS+1) rounded (not twice the largest finite) and hardware multiply/multiply_add may raise flags; the old prose also omitted the exp_lo <= 0 return. dyadic_float.h:284-400.

name: operator""_u8, operator""_u16, operator""_u32, operator""_u64
prose: Four LIBC_INLINE constexpr user-defined literal operators in namespace LIBC_NAMESPACE_DECL, each taking unsigned long long value: operator""_u8 returns static_cast<uint8_t>(value), _u16 returns static_cast<uint16_t>(value), _u32 returns static_cast<uint32_t>(value) and _u64 returns static_cast<uint64_t>(value). The result is the value reduced modulo 2^8, 2^16, 2^32 and 2^64 respectively; only _u64 returns the value unchanged on platforms where unsigned long long is 64 bits.
note: Old prose claimed the result is a uint64_t equal to the argument for all four; wrong for the narrower ones (integer_literals.h:26-40).

name: RwLock::unlock
prose: Member function returning LockResult (marked [[nodiscard]]). It loads the lock state with relaxed ordering. If a writer is active: if writer_tid (relaxed load) differs from internal::gettid() it returns PermissionDenied with no state change; otherwise it stores 0 to writer_tid (relaxed), clears the active-writer bit with an atomic fetch with release ordering, and returns Success at once if the previous state had no pending waiters. Else if readers are active: it decrements the reader count with release ordering (no check that the caller holds a read lock) and returns Success at once unless the previous state had the last reader and pending waiters. If neither a writer nor a reader is active it returns PermissionDenied. In the remaining cases it calls notify_pending_threads() (wakes writers if any are pending, otherwise readers) and returns Success.
note: Reviewers right: round 2 (reader path has no ownership check; the old prose said so but also had 'precondition none' in the contract); round 15 (the writer_tid store is relaxed, only the state fetch is release, rwlock.h:524-528).

name: TSSKeyMgr::remove_key
prose: Member function taking unsigned int key and returning bool: if key >= TSS_KEY_COUNT (1024) it returns false without touching any slot; otherwise it locks the manager's mutex (lock_guard, released on return), calls units[key].reset(), which sets active to false and dtor to nullptr, and returns true. It does not check whether the slot was active.
note: Contract cleared because the function mutates state under a mutex (reviewer right that the formal omitted the reset effect).

name: ranges::__move::operator() (iterator overload)
prose: Constexpr const call operator of ranges::__move taking (_InIter __first, _Sent __last, _OutIter __result), enabled for input_iterator _InIter, sentinel_for<_InIter> _Sent, weakly_incrementable _OutIter with indirectly_movable<_InIter, _OutIter>. It calls __move_impl, which forwards to std::__move<_RangeAlgPolicy>(first, last, result) and repackages the returned pair into a move_result<_InIter, _OutIter>: .in is the input iterator that reached the end of the range (an _InIter, equal to the end position) and .out is the output iterator after the last element written. The elements of [first, last) are moved into [result, ...); the destination must have room for them.
note: Round-15 reviewer's point (dangling) applies only to the range overload; for this iterator overload .in is an _InIter. Source ranges_move.h:46-51.

name: ranges::__move::operator() (range overload)
prose: Constexpr const call operator of ranges::__move taking (_Range&& __range, _OutIter __result), enabled for input_range _Range, weakly_incrementable _OutIter with indirectly_movable<iterator_t<_Range>, _OutIter>. It calls __move_impl(ranges::begin(__range), ranges::end(__range), result) and returns it as move_result<borrowed_iterator_t<_Range>, _OutIter>. The elements of the range are moved to successive positions from __result. .out is the output iterator after the last element written. .in is the iterator at the end of the range converted to borrowed_iterator_t<_Range>: that is a real iterator when the range type is a borrowed range, and a ranges::dangling object when it is not (for example an rvalue container).
note: Round-15 reviewer right for this overload (dangling for non-borrowed ranges). Source ranges_move.h:53-58.

name: ranges::__move_backward::operator() (iterator overload)
prose: Constexpr const call operator of ranges::__move_backward taking (_InIter __first, _Sent __last, _OutIter __result), enabled for bidirectional_iterator _InIter, sentinel_for<_InIter> _Sent, bidirectional_iterator _OutIter with indirectly_movable<_InIter, _OutIter>. It calls std::__move_backward<_RangeAlgPolicy>(first, last, result) through __move_backward_impl and returns move_backward_result<_InIter, _OutIter>: .in is the input iterator that reached the end of the range (an _InIter at the end position, not the sentinel itself when _Sent differs from _InIter) and .out is the output iterator at the beginning of the destination range. Elements are moved starting from the last, into the destination range ending at __result; __result must not lie inside (first, last].
note: Round-15 reviewer right: .in is the iterator at the end position, not necessarily __last when it is a different sentinel type. Source ranges_move_backward.h:48-53.

name: ranges::__move_backward::operator() (range overload)
prose: Constexpr const call operator of ranges::__move_backward taking (_Range&& __range, _Iter __result), enabled for bidirectional_range _Range, bidirectional_iterator _Iter with indirectly_movable<iterator_t<_Range>, _Iter>. It calls __move_backward_impl(ranges::begin(__range), ranges::end(__range), result) and returns move_backward_result<borrowed_iterator_t<_Range>, _Iter>: .in is the iterator at the end of the range converted to borrowed_iterator_t<_Range> (a ranges::dangling object when the range is not a borrowed range) and .out is the output iterator at the beginning of the destination range. Elements are moved starting from the last into the destination range ending at __result.
note: Round-15 reviewer right in that .in is an iterator (not a sentinel), or dangling. Source ranges_move_backward.h:55-60.

name: ranges::__next_permutation::operator() (iterator/sentinel overload)
prose: Constexpr const call operator of ranges::__next_permutation taking (_Iter __first, _Sent __last, _Comp __comp = {}, _Proj __proj = {}), enabled for bidirectional_iterator _Iter, sentinel_for<_Iter> _Sent and sortable<_Iter, _Comp, _Proj>. It calls std::__next_permutation<_RangeAlgPolicy>(first, last, projected comparison) and returns next_permutation_result<_Iter> {.in = the iterator it returned (the iterator at the end of the range), .found = the bool it returned}. The range is rearranged into the next lexicographic permutation under __comp and __proj and .found is true if there was one; otherwise the range is left in its first (sorted ascending) permutation and .found is false.
note: Round-15 reviewer's dangling point applies only to the range overload; here .in is an _Iter. Source ranges_next_permutation.h:44-51.

name: ranges::__next_permutation::operator() (range overload)
prose: Constexpr const call operator of ranges::__next_permutation taking (_Range&& __range, _Comp __comp = {}, _Proj __proj = {}), enabled for bidirectional_range _Range and sortable<iterator_t<_Range>, _Comp, _Proj>. It calls std::__next_permutation on begin and end of the range and returns next_permutation_result<borrowed_iterator_t<_Range>>: .in is the end iterator of the range converted to borrowed_iterator_t<_Range> (a ranges::dangling object for a non-borrowed range such as an rvalue container) and .found is true when the range was rearranged to the next lexicographic permutation; otherwise the range is left sorted in the first permutation and .found is false.
note: Round-15 reviewer right for this overload. Source ranges_next_permutation.h:53-60.

name: __mul_overflowed
prose: Four overloads in namespace __itoa (all inline, constexpr since C++23). (1) __mul_overflowed(unsigned char __a, _Tp __b, unsigned char& __r) computes __c = __a * __b in the promoted type, stores __c truncated to unsigned char in __r and returns __c > numeric_limits<unsigned char>::max(). (2) The same for unsigned short with unsigned short& __r. (3) Generic __mul_overflowed(_Tp __a, _Tp __b, _Tp& __r) static_asserts that _Tp is unsigned and returns __builtin_mul_overflow(__a, __b, &__r): true exactly when the exact product does not fit in _Tp, with __r holding the product reduced modulo 2^N in both cases. (4) __mul_overflowed(_Tp __a, _Up __b, _Tp& __r) casts __b to _Tp and calls the matching one of the first three. The old static-assert precondition applies only to overload (3).
note: Both reviewers right: the static_assert belongs to the generic overload only, and the unsigned char/short overloads compare against their own maxima (traits.h:116-141).

name: __convert_to_tm(const _Date& __date, chrono::weekday __weekday) [date/weekday overload]
prose: Template (requires _Date to be chrono::year_month_day or year_month_day_last; C++20) returning a zero-initialised _Tm (tm_zone = "UTC" under __GLIBC__) with tm_year = int(year) - 1900, tm_mon = unsigned(month) - 1, tm_mday = unsigned(day), tm_wday = __weekday.c_encoding() and tm_yday = the day count from January 1 of that year to the date (computed with sys_days arithmetic, no time_t conversion). It reads the date as given (an invalid date gives whatever the conversions produce) and contains no throw.
note: convert_to_tm.h:68-85

name: __convert_to_tm(const chrono::sys_time<_Duration> __tp) [sys_time overload]
prose: Template returning _Tm: floors __tp to days, builds the year_month_day and weekday and obtains the date fields through the date/weekday overload; then it takes the time since that midnight truncated to seconds as uint64_t, reduces it modulo 24*3600 and sets tm_hour, tm_min and tm_sec by division and remainder. Fractions of a second are dropped. It contains no throw.
note: convert_to_tm.h:87-103

name: __convert_to_tm(chrono::utc_time<_Duration> __tp) [utc_time overload]
prose: Template (compiled only when time zone database, filesystem, localization and experimental tzdb support are enabled) returning _Tm: converts __tp with utc_clock::to_sys to a sys_time and uses the sys_time overload, then increments tm_sec if chrono::get_leap_second_info(__tp).is_leap_second is true, so a leap second gives tm_sec one higher than the converted value (60).
note: convert_to_tm.h:108-116

name: __convert_to_tm(chrono::tai_time<_Duration> __tp) [tai_time overload]
prose: Template (same conditional compilation as the utc overload) returning _Tm: with _Rp = common_type_t<_Duration, seconds> it forms sys_time<_Rp>{__tp.time_since_epoch() - 4383 days expressed in seconds} (the TAI-to-UNIX epoch offset) and converts that with the sys_time overload; no leap-second table is consulted.
note: convert_to_tm.h:118-126

name: __convert_to_tm(chrono::gps_time<_Duration> __tp) [gps_time overload]
prose: Template (same conditional compilation as the utc overload) returning _Tm: converts with gps_clock::to_utc then utc_clock::to_sys and returns the sys_time overload's result; no leap-second increment is applied to tm_sec.
note: convert_to_tm.h:128-131

name: __convert_to_tm(const _ChronoT& __value) [generic dispatcher]
prose: Template returning _Tm, starting from a zero-initialised _Tm (tm_zone = "UTC" under __GLIBC__), choosing a branch at compile time. Time points: file_clock goes through clock::to_sys, local_t reuses the time since epoch as a sys_time; any other clock hits a static_assert (unless it has its own overload). Durations: only the time-of-day fields are set (via hours/seconds when convertible to hours, else seconds modulo 24*3600). day, month, year, weekday, weekday_indexed/last, month_day, month_day_last, month_weekday(_last) and year_month set only the corresponding tm fields; year_month_day(_last) and year_month_weekday(_last) delegate to the date/weekday overload; hh_mm_ss sets sec, min, hour and, when the hours representation is wider than tm_hour, throws format_error if hours exceed the int maximum; sys_info and local_info (tzdb builds) set nothing; zoned_time converts its local time as a sys_time. Any other type fails a static_assert at compile time.
note: convert_to_tm.h:138-230; old prose correct in outline, added the time-point and duration details.
